Background: In YTS we have a way to pop the controls out of the wall onto a tablet. This was intended primarily for VR users, but I watch people use it on desktop all the time. 

While our tablet is usable on desktop without major issues, it's basically mutually incompatible with TPV, since your avatar blocks the ability to see what you're holding (the tablet screen in this case, see attached image). Compounding this issue is the held item's distance adjustment overriding the scroll wheel, so the user is not even able to zoom into FPV to use the tablet unless they drop it and pick it up again afterwards.

I would like to have a way to detect if the user is in TPV, so we could gracefully degrade the tablet and any similar pickups.
title: Provide an Udon API to know if the user is in TPV

details:
Audio in the starter stage for third person seems to be based on avatar location and orientation. I'm sure this is a temporary idea, but I'd like to offer my suggestion that I think the best balanced way to implement this in the final version is to keep the audio sounding as it does from the avatar's head, but track the *direction* based on the camera.

I was spinning the avatar around and it was quite silly hearing the audio change as if I was spinning, when my camera was not. I thought maybe attaching the audio listener to the camera position *and* orientation would make sense at first, but honestly I think that has a higher chance of breaking worlds and immersion if desktop uses can cheat the audio listener location by going into third person like that. I think binding the stereo balance to the camera rotation, while keeping the position locked to the avatar head, is going to result in the smoothest experience across all forms of movement in and out of third person.
title: Audio Balancing for 3P

details:
It would be very helpful for the growth of VRChat on desktop if the new third-person camera allowed us to move the mouse freely, click, and interact with world objects without the camera constantly following the cursor.

A simple toggle to decouple the camera from mouse movement in third-person mode, along with a scripting API option, would open a lot of possibilities for creators. We could finally make proper third-person experiences for desktop players: action games, platformers, RPG-style worlds, minigames with UI interaction, and more, all with intuitive mouse control instead of constant camera movement.

This would make VRChat much more attractive and accessible to new players who don’t own a VR headset and are looking for “classic” third-person gameplay on desktop. At the same time, these games and worlds would still work perfectly fine in first-person for VR users, so creators wouldn’t have to maintain two completely separate versions of their content.

In short, giving us a way to temporarily disable mouse-driven camera movement in third-person — both as a user toggle and as a scripting feature — would greatly improve the desktop experience and encourage many more creators to build rich, game-like worlds for VRChat.
title: Option to decouple mouse from camera in third person

details:
While strictly over-the-shoulder third person is popular (e.g. Mass Effect), 'platformer' movement - where the camera orbits freely, and the player moves away from it when W is pressed, and toward it when S is pressed - is also popular (e.g. Breath of the Wild, It Takes Two, Helldivers 2). Typically, these games offer a way to quickly switch the camera control scheme between 'platformer' and 'over-the-shoulder' using on a button-hold or button toggle (usually for aiming weapons or items).

Currently in Build 1750, Tab only allows the camera to orbit the player until the player begins walking. If it's pressed while the player is already walking, the player's movement direction does not respect the camera direction, i.e. 'tank controls' (A and D turn the player, instead of making the player run to the left or right).
title: 'Platformer' 3rd-Person Control (camera-angle-based movement)

details:
Hello, here is my feedback on the third-person beta:

F5 as the default toggle feels out of place, since it’s widely used for refresh/reload in browsers, Windows Explorer, and even some world content (e.g., ProTV). A different default key would avoid conflicts with some existing content.

Desktop item holding: the usual scroll functionality is lost unless Alt is pressed. I suggest keeping scroll as-is, and using "ALT + SCROLL" to trigger third person. When the camera is adjusted, movement keys (WASD) should remain relative to the character, not force rotation toward a direction.

Camera controls: holding down "Alt" while in third person using the mouse could serve as an alternate easy way for moving the camera (instead of the hard switch with Tab).  

   + "SHIFT + ALT + SCROLL WHEEL" could handle vertical camera movement.  

   + "ALT + MIDDLE MOUSE" could adjust view angles/shoulder perspective.

I understand these bindings won’t suit everyone, but since interaction prompts are already included, they could help guide users through new alternative controls without confusion, better I say something than nothing I suppose.
title: Default Keys/Keybinds Feedback PC

# Issue:

Currently to enter free look mode you press Tab once and to exit you just start moving.

This how has some weird quirks to it:

- When enabling free look while walking, you can only disable it by standing still for a second. 

- Pressing Tab while already being in free look and walking results in the character snapping into your current view direction.

The free look enter / exit mechanic should be reworked to be more consistent. 

**There are 2 ways I could see this being done:**

1. Toggle Free Look: In this mode you would just press the button to toggle free look on / off.

2. Hold Free Look: In this mode you would have to hold the button to be in free look, once you let go you would automatically exit it again.

details:
Going into 3rd Person, invoking "Immobilize" from VRC Animator Locomotion Control, then pressing tab to free-rotate the camera, then pressing tab *again* causes a multitude of unusual behaviours.

- The first time tab is pressed, the camera unlocks and you can rotate around your avatar normally.

- The second time tab is pressed, the avatar's head snaps to the direction you were looking in (correctly) but its *body* *does not*, instead remains pointing the same way it did before

- Pressing tab a third time causes the avatar's head to snap to the direction your camera was facing, *plus the difference between the current rotation and the last time you hit tab*. The body still remains unmoved.

- Continuously pressing tab causes these rotations to add up and your avatars head to snap to seemingly random directions, until Immobilize is disabled.

- Other actions that cause the head to start following the camera's direction, such as exiting third person (by scrolling all the way up, pressing F5, etc) have a similar effect to pressing tab here.

In addition to Immobilize locking one axis of the camera, this now also makes your avatar look like it has its head screwed on backwards.
title: Immobilize + Tab causes camera to spin

details:
Currently a person can zoom in and out, as well as hit tab to enter orbit camera when standing still. However after walking forward while there is a camera orbiting, the player model snaps to where the camera is facing and walks forward with lock-strafe. This exits the camera orbiting mode.

As of writing this post, there is a way to press tab while already walking forwards to temporarily turn off lock-strafe and enable both camera orbiting and a 'free walking' mode where the player model turns around without the lock-strafe. Once the player model is still and stops walking, the lock-strafe returns.

My suggestion here as a feature request is that this should be a real option, if at all possible, to have a proper on/off toggle or keyboard binding that will allow people to have the ability to choose between the two player model walking behaviors. (Or at least, not have it auto-exit camera orbit when not walking.)

Since it is already possible in the game through tab when walking forwards, why not make it more official? The current implementation feels usable yet temporary. I can't say there would be many use cases, I personally think it'd be cool, like playing a video game.
title: Option for switching the walking behaviors during the third-person view.

details:
Another user can free-move (Tab) the 3rd person camera very close to you as long as there are no colliders between you - range seems to be about 5x avatar height. If you're within that range, they can get up close without you knowing, and while the scroll wheel may have discrete steps, moving their avatar allows precise camera positioning arbitrarily close.

Photo/stream cameras already get a visible indicator for similar reasons.

Idea: maybe if their camera is much closer to another player's avatar than it is to them, apply one or more of:

* show an icon (camera-style) to that player

* don't render the too-close avatar in the 3rd person view (personal space style) (edit: maybe prioritising hips given the possible sensitivity)

* force the avatar render layer's clipping plane to the same effect — though this without point (2) could allow for strategic clipping and would be more disruptive to screenshots
title: 3rd person cameras make undetectable close-up views of other players trivial
